subject: Re: SlateCo MSA — governing law, injunctive relief, and jurisdiction alignment
messages:
From: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@slateco.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: SlateCo MSA — proposed redlines (governing law / equitable relief)

Neha — attaching our mark of the MSA with a few focused concerns around dispute resolution. High level: SlateCo is pushing for Delaware governing law and mandatory arbitration with JAMS, plus a carve for emergency injunctive relief to be heard in a local state court (their position is we can 'consent to lift' only for immediate relief). They also want a mutual choice-of-law clause limited to contracts governed by Delaware law.

Attached: SlateCo_MSA_redlines_20261029.docx (track changes)

Key asks from our side: can Redwood accept Delaware law, but we need clarity on venue for urgent injunctive relief and whether arbitral proceedings can be stayed / interlocutory relief is permitted. Also, they propose a shorter discovery/filing limitation in arbitration (30 days) which looks aggressive.

Suggest a call tomorrow if that helps.

—Alan

Subject: Re: SlateCo MSA — proposed redlines (governing law / equitable relief)

Alan — thanks for sending. I reviewed the redline and pulled a short internal note attached. High-level reaction: Redwood can be flexible on governing law (we're fine with Delaware for commercial terms), but we need two clarifications before we can move forward: 

1) Emergency injunctive relief: we want an explicit carve that allows either party to seek provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction without waiving arbitration. Our legal team prefers language that preserves the right to seek temporary restraining orders or preliminary injunctions in federal or state court, plus an agreement that such filings don't waive the arbitration agreement.

2) Arbitration mechanics: JAMS is okay but the 30-day condensed timeline is too short. Propose a 90-day initial schedule with a fast-track option tied to a monetary threshold.

Kimberly — could you review the proposed carve language I drafted (see attached Redwood_Response_Summary_20261030.pdf) and call out any compliance / export-control concerns? Karthik — can you confirm whether a Delaware choice of law creates any product liability exposure we should flag to sales? Laura — if we hit a hard pushback on the injunctive carve, I may flag to you for escalation.

If helpful, let's set a 30-minute call tomorrow morning Pacific to walk through the compromises.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: SlateCo MSA — proposed redlines (governing law / equitable relief)

Neha / team — quick technical note from product/legal perspective: Delaware choice of law is acceptable from a contractual/enforceability lens and is common for our deals. The main product exposure is around injunctive relief that seeks to order changes to runtime behavior (e.g., block model access). If the injunctive carve is broad and permits immediate takedowns, that could impact our customers. Recommend: keep the injunctive carve narrow — \"provisional measures to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent and irreparable harm\" — and add explicit language that any remedy seeking to materially alter service must follow escalation / SLA procedures and notice.

Also, about arbitration: we should resist any clause that prevents interim relief prior to appointment of the arbitrator. Suggest redline that confirms interim relief is permissible and does not displace emergency court access.

Happy to discuss on the call.

—Karthik
Director, Product Legal (Contracts)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateCo MSA — proposed redlines (governing law / equitable relief)

Team — reviewed the draft carve and the quick notes. A couple of practical points from security/compliance: 

- Any injunctive language that contemplates "immediate access to logs or systems" must be scoped tightly and tied to a subpoena or court order. We cannot provide unfettered real-time access.
- If we accept Delaware law, update the data retention / audit clause references to ensure they don't conflict with state-specific obligations (there are some differences in discovery scope).

Suggested language highlight (short): \"Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional or interlocutory relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm; such action shall not constitute a waiver of the arbitration agreement.\"

I'll join the call.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@slateco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateCo MSA — proposed redlines (governing law / equitable relief)

Alan — thanks for the quick turnaround. Proposed next steps: 

1) We can accept Delaware as governing law for the MSA.
2) Redwood requests an express carve allowing either party to pursue provisional/interlocutory relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent irreparable harm; such filings will not constitute a waiver of the parties' arbitration obligation.
3) Arbitration timeline: propose 90 days as default with a documented fast-track option for disputes under $250k.

If SlateCo agrees to the above, we can incorporate the language and provide a clean copy for signature. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call today at 1pm PT to finalize. If that time doesn't work, suggest 10:00am PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Neha
